notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Tuesday 3 November (EGX30 49,255.66). Brent is Tuesday's settlement. US midterm results are projections from election night, not certified counts. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.

items: Brent falls 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday, its biggest drop in three months, after Iran's supreme leader approves talks and Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound, though a US strike on Qeshm Island overnight lifts Brent 0.5% in Asia.

The pound strengthens to EGP 55.51 per dollar at the CBE on Monday from 56.12 after the hike, and major banks quote 55.49 → the 100 bp hike and falling oil ease demand for dollars; a firmer pound helps importers and foreign holders of local debt.

EGX30 slips 0.70% to 48,403.14 while the EGX70 and EGX100 fall more than 2.2% and 197 stocks decline against 31 → foreigners net sell EGP 138.1 mn and Banque du Caire absorbs 21% of turnover, leaving little cash for small caps.

Banque du Caire closes its first session at EGP 5.31, up 0.19% on the EGP 5.30 offer, after touching EGP 5.68 → pricing at fair value leaves little first-day gain; the Treasury takes up to half the EGP 36.37 bn proceeds to ease debt.

Egypt's non-oil PMI stays at 47.2 in October, below a 48 forecast and its tenth straight month below 50 → output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months and input costs rise at a five-month high.

EGX30 falls 1.72% to 48,744.01 in the first session after the hike, with 148 stocks down and only 63 up as Palm Hills drops 7% → higher rates hit developers and consumer lenders while foreign and Arab investors sell; turnover of EGP 7.2 bn is 35% below its 90-day average.

Banque du Caire starts trading today as BQDC at an offer price of EGP 5.30, after a record EGP 205.8 bn of private-placement orders → the debut tests demand in a falling market; retail holders can sell back at EGP 5.30 for 30 days through CI Capital.

The state borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home in July to October, almost all to refinance, and a finance official says the hike adds EGP 150 bn to the bill → short-dated debt reprices fast, so the 100 bp move feeds straight into the budget; the first post-hike 364-day bill sells at 26.076%.

Brent falls about 3.2% to $109.75 early Monday after Iran says a Qatari-brokered plan could reopen Hormuz within two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's import bill, but Trump still talks of hitting one or two more targets after Tuesday's midterms.

AMOC reports quarterly sales up 41% to EGP 43.2 bn and net profit up 154% to EGP 3.475 bn → high oil prices and refining margins lift results; the stock rises 2.21% on Sunday against a falling market.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Iran says Hormuz stays shut and there are no nuclear talks until the US meets its demands, as one report says US strikes could come as early as 4 November → the risk of a wider war after the midterms keeps oil, shipping and regional risk premiums high as the EGX reopens.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The pound holds at EGP 56.12 per dollar at the CBE as banks open Sunday at 56.04–56.19 to sell, the first quotes after the hike → the hike has not yet moved the pound, so today's EGX session tests how equities price higher rates.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income and the carry trade but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The S&P 500 falls 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Friday after Intel's outlook, while gold drops 3.52% to $3,879.90 → a risk-off week end and forced selling of metals weigh on sentiment toward emerging markets before the EGX reopens.

Qatari mediators in Tehran deliver a Vance letter proposing a new diplomatic process, with a meeting possible within a week in Doha or Istanbul → talks offer a path away from escalation, but reports say Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the midterms.

The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate after Thursday's close, its first hike since March 2024, against a Reuters poll that expected a hold → the pound near record lows at EGP 56.12 and heavy foreign selling of local debt push the CBE to defend the carry trade; Sunday is the EGX's first session to price it.

EGX30 rises 0.64% to 49,596.14 on Thursday as Banque du Caire's EGP 36.37 bn offering executes and lifts turnover to EGP 43.9 bn → foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn, mostly through the bank's offering, while 180 stocks rise and 31 fall before trading in BQDC starts on 2 November.

The IMF targets a staff-level deal on Egypt's final review before mid-December, worth about $2.3 bn in final disbursements → Kozack says talks focus on tight monetary policy, which the CBE's hike now delivers.

Brent rises 1.04% to $116.08 in early Friday trade after settling at $114.88 on Thursday, as a tanker is hit in Hormuz and US strike talk returns → oil near $116 widens Egypt's fuel import bill while pump prices stay frozen.

The ECB and the Bank of Japan both hold, the BoJ at 1.25% by 8-1, while Reuters sources call a 17 December ECB hike all but certain → global policy stays tight after US growth beats forecasts at 3.4%, limiting appetite for emerging-market debt.

key.l: projected Democratic House seats, per CNBC

stories.h: Democrats win the House and Senate in a rebuke to Trump
stories.what: Democrats are projected to win at least 245 House seats, well above the 218 needed, and at least 51 Senate seats, CNBC's election desk says. Democrats flip Republican Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas, and Troy Jackson is projected to beat Susan Collins in Maine. Trump tells The New York Times he is willing to accept the results.
stories.why: Coverage frames the vote as a rebuke of Trump; he says the losses were not about him.
stories.aff: US fiscal policy, war funding, the dollar and Treasury yields.
stories.eg: A Congress controlled by Democrats could restrain new military action against Iran, which matters for oil and Suez.
stories.egx: Neutral; the direct channel to the EGX runs through oil and the Iran talks.

stories.h: EGX30 rebounds 1.76% as foreign institutions buy and 180 stocks rise
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Youm7; Masrawy; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Tuesday at 49,255.66, up 1.76%, ending four straight sessions of declines; the EGX70 rises 2.18% and the EGX100 1.97%. 180 stocks rise and 29 fall on turnover of EGP 7.5 bn, 32.6% below the 90-day average. Orascom Development (+6.8%), Palm Hills (+6.8%) and Eastern Company (+6.1%) lead, while Abu Qir (-3.6%), Mopco (-3.0%) and Valmore (-2.5%) fall. Foreign institutions net buy EGP 136 mn and Egyptian individuals net sell EGP 169.8 mn.
stories.why: None of the sources gives a single cause; the pound firms and oil falls during the session.
stories.aff: Developers, consumer staples and foreign-held blue chips.
stories.eg: Market cap rises about EGP 52 bn to EGP 3.890 tn, Youm7 says.
stories.egx: Bullish for developers and blue chips; fertiliser names lag on gas cuts.
stories.names: Orascom Development, Palm Hills, Eastern Company (up); Abu Qir, Mopco, Valmore (down).

key.l: gas supply to fertilizer and methanol plants

stories.h: Gas to fertilizer plants is cut 20% as Egyptian urea climbs to $535
stories.what: Egyptian granular urea sells at about $535 a ton FOB in November contracts, up about 17% from $457 in September, making Egypt the most expensive origin. Kima says its gas supply is cut 20% from 1 November, and Abu Qir tells the EGX its gas load is reduced but it has flexibility to manage. CI Capital expects lower volumes at Abu Qir, Mopco and Valmore in 4Q and possibly 2027.
stories.why: Costly LNG imports force the state to ration gas to industry.
stories.aff: Fertiliser output, export earnings and farm input costs.
stories.eg: Chemical and fertilizer exports reach $9.54 bn in the first nine months of 2026, up 34%, so lower volumes would cost dollars.
stories.egx: Bearish for Abu Qir and Mopco on volumes, partly offset by higher urea prices.
stories.names: Abu Qir Fertilizers, Mopco, Valmore, Kima.

key.l: cost of one LNG import cargo, double September

stories.h: LNG cargoes cost over $100 mn each as the IEA sees a tight market into 2027
stories.what: Egypt asks suppliers for about 10 LNG cargoes in November, down from 12 in October, at over $100 mn each, putting the month's bill near $1 bn; it defers five cargoes into 2027. It also plans its first export cargo in months from Idku by end-November, worth over $60 mn. The IEA expects the regional war to remove about 150 bn cbm of LNG supply from 2026 to 2030.
stories.why: Damage to Qatar's Ras Laffan and delays to new projects keep supply short, while imports now cover nearly half of Egypt's gas use.
stories.aff: The import bill, reserves, the budget's $10.7 bn gas import line and industry's gas supply.
stories.eg: Net LNG imports exceed domestic gas production for the first time in July, EnterpriseAM says.
stories.egx: Bearish for gas-dependent industry such as fertilisers, steel and cement.

stories.h: Brent settles at a four-week low as Iran calls the US reply unconvincing
stories.src: Reuters via Yahoo Finance; CBS News
stories.what: Brent settles $1.17 lower at $103.60, its lowest close since 7 October, and WTI 37 cents lower at $96.09. Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei calls the US response to Iran's seven demands not convincing, while Qatari mediators expect feedback on a new proposal within 36 hours. A cargo vessel is struck off Oman and an Indian-crewed dhow attacked in Hormuz, killing at least one mariner.
stories.why: Traders weigh talks to end the wars in Iran and Ukraine against fresh attacks on shipping; ING warns escalation risks may not be over.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill, the pound and inflation expectations.
stories.eg: Lower crude reduces the dollar cost of Egypt's fuel imports.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and energy users; bearish for oil-linked AMOC.

stories.h: Government weighs a large EgyptAlum stake sale on the EGX before year-end
stories.what: The state weighs selling a large stake in Egypt Aluminum on the EGX before the end of 2026, with the size set by a pending fair-value study. Metallurgical Industries Holding owns 89.84% and the public float is about 2.9% excluding state pension funds, by EnterpriseAM's calculation. The state targets $1.5 bn of offering proceeds before year-end, and Banque du Caire's sale brought in $658 mn.
stories.why: The divestment target is tied to Egypt's IMF commitments as the programme ends in December.
stories.aff: EGX liquidity, brokers and the state's asset-sale programme.
stories.eg: Asset sales bring dollars and cut the state's footprint, an IMF priority.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokers and for EGAL's liquidity; pricing is unknown.

key.l: CBE sell rate, EGP per USD, Tue 3 Nov

stories.h: Pound firms to 55.42 per dollar at the CBE
stories.what: The CBE's closing rate on Tuesday is 55.28 buy and 55.42 sell. National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr quote 55.29 and 55.39, and both outlets report the dollar lower at the close. The CBE's deposit rate stands at 20% after last week's hike.
stories.why: Higher rates and the fall in oil ease pressure on the pound; neither report gives a single cause.
stories.aff: Import costs, inflation expectations and foreign holders of local debt.
stories.eg: A firmer pound lowers the cost of imported fuel and food.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and foreign-held blue chips.

key.l: Qatar's window for feedback on its new proposal

stories.h: Iran calls the US reply unconvincing as Qatar waits for both sides' answers
stories.what: Mohsen Rezaei says America's response to Iran's demands was "not convincing" and its seven conditions must be met. Qatar says it remains hopeful of an interim deal and expects feedback within 36 hours. Iran says it keeps the right to self-defence after the US strikes on Qeshm Island, and a tanker is hit by two projectiles off Oman.
stories.why: The two sides remain far apart on sanctions relief and the US naval blockade.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: A deal would ease Egypt's energy costs and help Suez; escalation would do the opposite.
stories.egx: Neutral pending the next round of talks.

week.why: The first inflation print after the CBE's 100 bp hike; September urban inflation was 13.9%. CAPMAS usually publishes around the 9th or 10th.
